label: AI FOR HEALTHCARE
title: Understanding dementia. Predicting what comes next.
summary: Multimodal learning for earlier detection, disease progression, and fairer dementia classification.
problem: A dementia prediction model must answer more than a diagnostic question. Can it distinguish stages of cognitive impairment, estimate when progression may occur, and work across populations? Clinical assessments and brain images provide complementary evidence, but missing observations and population differences make learning difficult.
approach: This research brings together neuroimaging and clinical information through attention, multitask learning, and longitudinal models. The 2023 Scientific Reports study introduced stacked polynomial attention (SPAN) and adaptive exponential decay to jointly learn MCI stage and time to Alzheimer’s conversion. Related journal work explores bidirectional prediction with imputation, modality uncertainty, and fair and explainable dementia classification.

findings.title: Learning diagnosis and progression together
findings.text: On the ADNI cohort, the 2023 model reported a c-index of 0.85 for conversion-time prediction and 83.19% accuracy for MCI-stage classification. These are study results for that cohort.

findings.title: Making incomplete histories useful
findings.text: The 2022 Neural Networks paper combines forward-to-backward bidirectional learning with integrative imputation for longitudinal progression prediction.

findings.title: Extending the question to fairness
findings.text: The 2026 Nature Communications paper examines fair and explainable neuroimaging dementia pattern classification across racial and ethnic populations.

perspective: The common thread is to learn from complementary patient information while examining how reliable a prediction is, and for whom it works.

label: BRAIN HEALTH
title: Brain aging, beyond a single biomarker.
summary: Connecting brain networks, vascular burden, and population studies to understand brain health.
problem: Brain health reflects multiple interacting processes. Functional connectivity, structural brain changes, and vascular disease each describe a different aspect of aging. A useful research question is how these measurements can be studied together without reducing every change to one diagnosis.
approach: This theme groups collaborative journal work on machine learning biomarkers derived from a large functional-connectome collection and on brain small vessel disease in the SPRINT randomized clinical trial. It connects computational biomarker development with cohort-based clinical analysis.

findings.title: Studying aging through functional networks
findings.text: The 2026 Brain Research Bulletin paper derives machine learning brain-aging biomarkers from a collection of forty thousand functional connectomes.

findings.title: Examining vascular burden in a trial setting
findings.text: The 2026 eClinicalMedicine paper examines overall brain small vessel disease burden in a post-hoc analysis of intensive versus standard blood pressure control in SPRINT.

perspective: These papers address complementary measurements of brain health. The source articles provide the study designs, effect estimates, and limitations for each investigation.

blog_summary: Brain aging is reflected in networks, anatomy, vascular health, and population-level variation. This research connects machine-learning biomarkers derived from large functional-connectome datasets with clinical studies of cerebral small-vessel disease and blood-pressure control.
research_at_glance: Functional-connectome modeling investigates machine-learning brain-aging biomarkers.
The SPRINT publication examines brain small-vessel disease burden in a post-hoc trial analysis.

label: HUMAN-CENTERED AI
title: Understanding emotion in context.
summary: Learning from voices, faces, language, and social relationships to understand affective behavior.
problem: Emotion is expressed across channels, and the meaning of a cue can change with context. A voice, a facial expression, and a spoken sentence may reinforce or contradict one another. Conversations and group interactions add dependencies between people and over time.
approach: The journal papers explore multi-head attention for speech emotion, deep graph fusion for evoked expressions, cross-modality interactions for emotion reasoning, and relation-aware graph-recurrent learning in conversations. The GCE dataset extends the work to group cohesion and emotion analysis.

findings.title: Moving from separate signals to interactions
findings.text: Attention and graph-based models explicitly learn relationships between modalities and contextual representations, rather than treating each channel as an isolated prediction task.

findings.title: Representing conversational context
findings.text: The residual relation-aware model studies emotion recognition in conversation through graph-recurrent learning.

findings.title: Studying people together
findings.text: The GCE journal publication contributes an audio-visual dataset for investigating group cohesion and emotion.

perspective: Across these studies, the central contribution is the representation of complementary signals and their relationships. Each paper reports evaluations on its own datasets and tasks.

research_at_glance: Attention and fusion methods investigate relationships between complementary input channels.
Graph-recurrent research brings relational and conversational context into modeling.
The GCE publication introduces an audio-visual dataset for group cohesion and emotion analysis.

label: MEDICAL VISION
title: From an image to a meaningful region.
summary: Segmentation and semi-supervised learning for bone tumors and abnormal tissue analysis.
problem: Medical images contain structures that matter differently to a diagnostic task. Learning a classifier from limited labeled images can be difficult when the relevant anatomy occupies only a small part of the image, or when normal tissue obscures an abnormal region.
approach: This work connects segmentation with classification. The knee bone tumor study uses a regenerative semi-supervised bidirectional W-network guided by three-region bone segmentation. A related journal paper enhances U-Net with a spatial-channel attention gate for abnormal tissue segmentation.

findings.title: Using anatomy to guide classification
findings.text: The W-network study integrates three-region bone segmentation into the knee bone tumor classification pipeline.

findings.title: Attending to relevant spatial and channel features
findings.text: The U-Net study investigates a spatial-channel attention gate for abnormal tissue segmentation in medical images.

perspective: The shared idea is to make the region representation part of the learning problem. The publications provide the validation settings and performance comparisons.

blog_summary: When labeled medical images are limited, knowing where a model should look can be as important as the classifier itself. This work connects segmentation, attention, reconstruction, and semi-supervised learning to extract more meaningful representations from medical images.
research_at_glance: The W-network study connects three-region bone segmentation with radiograph classification.
The U-Net study investigates spatial-channel attention for abnormal-tissue segmentation.
Segmentation and classification have different outputs and require task-specific evaluations.

label: SENSING & INTERACTION
title: Turning everyday signals into interaction.
summary: Smartphone motion, depth cameras, and connected systems for localization and natural interaction.
problem: Everyday sensors are noisy, and the way a person moves changes the signal. A smartphone must estimate a walking path despite varying speed and arm swing. A depth camera must distinguish useful gestures and fingertips from background movement.
approach: The journal work explores adaptive step detection and step-length estimation for smartphone pedestrian dead reckoning, nonparametric estimation for arm-swing walking, RGB-D hand gesture recognition, and a fingertip-driven virtual mouse. Earlier wireless-network research examines relay selection under channel estimation error.

findings.title: Adapting to the person’s movement
findings.text: The smartphone studies address variable walking speeds and arm-swing walking through adaptive and regression-based step-length estimation.

findings.title: Connecting perception with an interface
findings.text: RGB-D studies investigate real-time hand gesture spotting and fingertip detection for a virtual mouse system.

findings.title: Accounting for imperfect measurements
findings.text: The relay-selection paper studies the impact of channel estimation error in cognitive radio networks, an earlier foundation in signal analysis.

perspective: These projects share an interest in building useful estimates and interfaces from imperfect measurements in everyday settings.
